images.title: Common factors of 12 and 16
images.purpose: Sort the factors of 12 and 16 into a Venn diagram so the common factors, and the largest one, stand out.
images.composition: One two-circle Venn diagram fills the centre of the frame with generous white space around it.
exact_structure: Left circle outlined and lightly tinted teal (#0072B2), headed Factors of 12 above it.
Right circle outlined and lightly tinted amber (#E69F00), headed Factors of 16 above it.
Left only region holds exactly 3 numbers: 3, 6, 12.
Right only region holds exactly 2 numbers: 8, 16.
The number 4 in the overlap has a reddish purple (#CC79A7) ring around it and is slightly larger than the other numbers.
The small word largest sits just below the overlap with a short reddish purple (#CC79A7) pointer to the ringed 4.
Each number appears exactly once in the whole diagram; 8 numbers in total.
rejection: any number placed in the wrong region, or any of 1, 2, 4 outside the overlap
any extra number such as 5 or 32, or any number repeated
a ring around any number other than 4
images.takeaway: The common factors 1, 2, 4 are the tile sizes that fit, and the largest, 4, gives the fewest tiles.
images.description: A Venn diagram with factors of 12 and of 16; the overlap holds 1, 2 and 4, with 4 ringed as the largest.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Read the overlap first, then ask why the ringed number is the best tile size.

image_decisions.why: A Venn diagram makes the idea of a common factor visible at a glance.
